title: Outcomes linked to decisions: what number followed each decision, judged against its reference
request: Phase 1's gap: a decision was recorded with its answers and labels but never with what it led to. Every decision of a project should carry the outcome that followed (the final stage's holdout, a promotion, a business number a person typed), the decision sets should carry it, and the Decisions tab should show how each point turned out; adoptable by the main product.
spec: dclab_core.outcomes.Outcome v1 with judge/join/by_point; outcome.observed events (contract v6); written by the final stage, the final stage's approval and POST /api/projects/{id}/outcome for every decision of the project; stored append-only (files or decision_outcome, migration 0018) and deleted with the project; the decision export carries them without a person's note; datasets.decisions rows gain outcome and datasets.outcome_labels is a set of its own; the Admin Decisions tab counts well/badly/none per point; adapters.main_product_outcomes maps an experiments row's result.
plan: Contract and rule in dclab_core: Outcome, judge (a holdout within a tolerance of its CV estimate turned out well), join, by_point.
A store per backend, append-only like the ledger's other tables; retention removes a project's rows.
Write where the number is observed: the final stage, its approval, a route for a business number; one event per observation.
Carry it out: export, decision sets, an outcome_labels set, the Decisions tab.
Adapter: experiments.result onto the decisions linked to the experiment; model_versions listed as missing.

decisions.decision: Every decision of the project gets the project's outcome, not only the final stage's.
decisions.why: A number follows every choice that shaped the pipeline; which ones mattered is what a model may learn from the set.

decisions.decision: The verdict compares the holdout to the chosen model's cross-validation mean within a tolerance (0.02 for a bounded metric, 5% otherwise).
decisions.why: An honest model holds its estimate; a holdout far below it says the decisions before it misled.

decisions.decision: An outcome is never a label and effective_label never reads it.
decisions.why: It says what followed, not what was right: a good number can follow a leak.

decisions.decision: A promotion is the final stage approved; there is no rejection in this product.
decisions.why: The product has no model registry; the main product's model_versions is the place for both.

decisions.decision: The export drops a person's note outright.
decisions.why: Free text has no place in a set; the number and the verdict are what the set needs.

decisions.decision: The experience event moves to v6 and the dataset manifest to v3.
decisions.why: A kind and a builder value are part of a contract's shape (the rule since 23.2).

change: dclab_core outcomes.py (new), experience.py (kind, v6), datasets.py (outcome column, outcome_labels, manifest v3), schemas.py, adapters/main_product_outcomes.py (new), adapters/main_product_experience.py (KINDS_MISSING), CHANGELOG 0.42.0; dclab_rnd ledger/outcomes.py (new), ledger/__init__.py (the stores' add_outcome/outcomes), storage/models.py + migration 0018, experience/retention.py, studio/engine.py (final stage, approval), agentic/routers/projects.py (the route), ledger/labels.py (summary), consent.py (export), datasets.py (build), web admin.html; tests test_outcomes.py (new), test_experience_log, test_datasets, test_consent (its stores opened the product's way), the version pins; CORE_INTEGRATION.md, the plan.

findings.defect: The gate on 23.4 failed under PostgreSQL: tests/test_consent.py built its PgLog bare, and since 23.3 a log with no folder stamps every record operate.
findings.scenario: ExportTest exported nothing on PostgreSQL; on files it passed because a FileLog knows its folder.
findings.cause: The test did not open its stores the product's way.
findings.fix: The test's stores() uses experience.open_log and ledger.open_ledger (the folder is set there).

findings.defect: An exported decision doc with its new outcomes key failed DecisionRecord validation in the set builders.
findings.scenario: datasets.decisions raised extra_forbidden; no decision set was built.
findings.fix: Every reader strips labels and outcomes.

findings.defect: The outcomes builder was not in the manifest's Builder vocabulary.
findings.fix: DatasetManifest v3 (v1, v2 read as v3).

findings.defect: Outcomes were written during a replay, into the real ledger.
findings.scenario: POST .../pipeline/rerun?step=stage:final replays the final stage on a scratch copy under experience.quiet(); observe() ignored the flag and appended a holdout outcome per decision of the real project, under the scratch run id; on PostgreSQL the rows cannot be removed.
findings.cause: decide(), label() and experience.record() check _QUIET; the new writer did not.
findings.fix: observe() returns early inside quiet(); the same for the event.

findings.defect: The newest observation won whatever it said: a promotion forced 'well' and an unjudged business number wrote 'unknown', both erasing a 'badly' holdout.
findings.scenario: Holdout 0.70 against a CV mean of 0.85 is badly; approving the final stage (how a project finishes) then wrote well for every decision, and the tab, the column and outcome_labels said well.
findings.cause: join and _current_outcome took the latest row; from_approval hard-coded the verdict.
findings.fix: The promotion is judged as the holdout was (its direction); one preference rule in dclab_core (judged before unjudged, business before the model's own, then newest) is used by join and the datasets.

findings.defect: Every project on a kind with its own machine got verdict unknown: the direction was read from a bundle those kinds do not have.
findings.scenario: Forecasting, ranking, anomaly, streams, entity tables, uplift, segmentation, embedded, time-to-event: rows written, all unknown, shown as 'no outcome yet'.
findings.cause: p.bundle.spec.higher_is_better only exists on the tabular Prepared.
findings.fix: _after_final reads machine.higher_is_better when the prepared object has a machine.

findings.defect: The file-to-PostgreSQL migration dropped a workspace's outcomes.
findings.scenario: python -m dclab_rnd.storage migrate copied records and labels only; outcomes are written once at the final stage and are not recreated.
findings.cause: The migration lists the ledger's tables by hand.
findings.fix: decision_outcomes copied beside the other two; the archive doc and the ledger docstring list the table.

findings.defect: Decisions made in the draft (family, workflow, cleaning) never got an outcome.
findings.scenario: Home's decisions carry draft= with no project; the done-when says every decision that shaped it.
findings.fix: The drafts that became the project are read too; retention removes the outcome rows by project as well.

findings.defect: The promotion rows never got the run id: the stage record's run holds the RunRecord whose field is run, not id.
findings.scenario: run was None in production; the test used an invented shape.
findings.test: the final-stage test builds the record in the real shape

findings.defect: A ledger error failed the final stage after the holdout was read.
findings.scenario: PostgreSQL briefly down: from_final raised inside _run_stage's try; the stage was marked failed with the holdout used.
findings.cause: The records read sat outside any try; every other capture call is wrapped.
findings.fix: from_final, from_approval and the reads never raise.
findings.test: covered by the wrapped bodies (no test: needs a failing ledger)

findings.defect: The route accepted non-finite numbers, a string for higher_is_better, a number before any final stage, and a free-text metric.
findings.scenario: value 'nan' answered 200 with nothing written; 'false' became True; 'retention of ACME Corp' left in the dataset rows.
findings.fix: 422 for non-finite numbers, a non-boolean direction and a metric that is not a slug; 409 before the final stage ran; the contract's metric is a slug; the permission is pinned (the default write: owner and ML engineer).

findings.defect: One transaction (or one file lock) per outcome row.
findings.scenario: A wide table has thousands of column decisions; the final stage and the approval each wrote that many single-row writes.
findings.test: the existing outcome tests through both stores

findings.defect: The engine hooks were untested, and nothing pinned that an outcome is never a label.
findings.cause: Tests called the writer on hand-built records.
findings.fix: test_decision_capture drives the real final stage and checks the holdout outcomes; the decision-set test asserts label is None for an outcome-only decision.

findings.defect: A metric was a person's free text (up to 80 characters) and left through the outcome docs.
findings.scenario: 'retention of ACME Corp' in an exported set.
findings.cause: The note was dropped, the metric was not.
findings.fix: The contract's metric is a slug.

findings.defect: The verdict compares points and ignores the interval; not said.
findings.scenario: A holdout below the CV mean with the reference inside its interval is 'badly'.
findings.fix: Said in the contract's docstring and the set's limits.

outcome: Every decision of a project carries what followed it, with its verdict; the sets and the Decisions tab show it; the main product maps its experiments' results the same way. Reviewed: 12 findings, all fixed or written down.
lessons: A test must open a store the product's way: a bare PostgreSQL log has no folder and no consent, and only the PostgreSQL pass shows it.
risks: Every decision of a project shares the project's outcome: a set that learns from it must group by project, as the splits do.
The main product's model_versions is not in the field lists read; a promotion outcome waits for 23.12.
